text.p: The Zimbabwean government is offering 75 percent of its shareholding in the national dairy, its first ever public sale of a state firm.
According to offer documents released on Thursday, 168.3 million Dairibord Zimbabwe Limited (DZL) shares are on offer at a price of Z$1.20 (U.S.$0.11) each.

The government, which has been under pressure from Western donors to privatise loss-making state firms, said the offer marked the final stage of transforming the dairy from a loss-maker to a profitable commercial enterprise.

Under the proposed new share structure, the public would hold 15 percent of the shares. A yet-to-be-identified technical partner would have 10 percent with an option to buy a further 15 percent of the company's equity from a remaining 40 percent stake held by the government.

The state National Investment Trust which was formed to promote the government's programme to economically empower the country's majority blacks, large-scale milk producers and DZL employees would hold 10 percent each. Small-scale producers would have five percent of the company's shares.
The government said a decision to list DZL shares on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange would rest with the directors of the privatised company.
But it said pending the listing, some selected stockbrokers would conduct an "over the counter" market in the company's shares after the close of the offer.
The offer opens on June 16 and closes on June 27.
